transcript.content:
Based on my analysis, the bug is in the `get_key_name` function in `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py`. 

The issue occurs because:

1. `fix_range_content_type` calls `get_key_name(path, headers)` to extract the key from the path
2. `get_key_name` uses `uses_path_addressing(headers)` to decide how to parse the path
3. On CircleCI (and possibly other environments), `uses_path_addressing` returns `False` because the host header doesn't match `HOSTNAME`, `HOSTNAME_EXTERNAL`, or `LOCALHOST_IP`
4. When it returns `False`, `get_key_name` returns `path_parts[0]` — which is the bucket name (`test-bucket`), not the object key
5. This causes `s3_client.head_object(Bucket='test-bucket', Key='test-bucket')` to make a HEAD request to `/test-bucket/test-bucket` (double bucket name)

The fix: when the path contains both bucket and key segments (i.e., `path_parts` has length > 1), the function should return `path_parts[1]` regardless of whether path addressing is detected, because in the context of the edge proxy, the path always includes the bucket name.
